paper_metadata.title: Preparing Arbitrary Continuous Functions in Quantum Registers With Logarithmic Complexity

summary: The paper presents a theoretical framework for preparing discretized continuous functions on quantum registers with query complexity O(F^p/ε^2), where p = -4 for pointwise encoding and p = -2 for integral encoding, and with O(n + d) ancilla qubits. It also gives two alternative circuit constructions: a phase-estimation-based normalization/state-preparation method using m ancilla qubits and a single-ancilla destructive-interference verifier, but all results are analytical or numerical simulations rather than hardware demonstrations.

experiments.description: Direct state preparation of discretized continuous functions via adiabatic evolution of a rank-1 Hamiltonian, demonstrated numerically on a log-normal distribution and a Slater-type function.

algorithm.variant: adiabatic state preparation using rank-1 Hamiltonian simulation and low-rank/1-sparse simulation subroutines
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared as uniform superposition |+>^⊗n; interpolated function fs=(1-s)f0+sf1 with f0 chosen as an easy-to-prepare constant function

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n qubits encode N=2^n grid points x_j on [a,b]; amplitudes proportional to samples f(x_j) (pointwise encoding) or to piecewise integrals g(x_j) (integral encoding)
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |ψ> ∝ Σ_j f(x_j)|j> (or integral-encoded analogue) for an arbitrary efficiently computable continuous function
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints; uses adiabatic interpolation and rank-1 projector Hamiltonian H(s) ∝ |ψ_s><ψ_s|
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(s) = -A(s)/N where A(s) is rank-1 with entries [A(s)]_kl = f_s(x_k) f_s*(x_l)
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: n + d + 2 ancillary qubits (reported as O(n+d))

problem_instance.description: Numerical demonstrations for preparing a log-normal probability density and a Slater-type orbital/wavefunction on a discretized interval

dataset_specification.description: Continuous functions on domain [0,1] used for numerical experiments; log-normal distribution and Slater function e^{-α|x-0.5|}

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Functions discretized on a uniform grid with N=2^n points; function values digitized to d-bit precision (example in appendix uses d=32 bits)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Large-scale numerical simulations of the exact 1-sparse simulation of the 2n-qubit system; state-preparation infidelity plotted versus number of qubits n and number of iterations r

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical evaluation of function values f(x) and digitization to d-bit precision; numerical simulation of the 1-sparse Hamiltonian evolution
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla in |+> basis and discard/reset; compute state-preparation infidelity and fit scaling versus r and n

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Infidelity decreases approximately polynomially with r; approaches constant in n

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical direct search or classical loading of all samples
speedup_claims.conditions: fault-tolerant gate-based quantum computer; efficiently computable continuous functions; constant filling ratio F; asymptotic in n
speedup_claims.caveats: Complexity depends inverse-polynomially on filling ratio F; pathological narrow functions can remove the advantage.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical evaluation over N=2^n grid points
speedup_claims.conditions: asymptotically in number of qubits for continuous functions
speedup_claims.caveats: Constant factor depends on F, target error ϵ, and simulation subroutine error.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(F^p / ϵ^2) query complexity for state preparation, with p = -4 for pointwise encoding and p = -2 for integral encoding; asymptotically constant in n
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical direct search for the pathological search-like instance is O(2^n); classical loading of all samples is O(N)
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Depends inverse-polynomially on filling ratio F; constant in n for continuous functions
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Constant number of oracle queries per timestep; total O(r) timesteps with r chosen to meet ϵ
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: O(N) function evaluations for full classical sampling/loading

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not assessed; no hardware benchmark or classical runtime crossover reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Asymptotic query complexity O(F^p / ε^2) with p = -4 (pointwise) or p = -2 (integral); O(n + d) ancilla qubits; constant in n for continuous functions.

experiments.description: Phase-estimation-based state preparation / normalization-factor estimation for continuous functions, presented as an alternative to the adiabatic method.

algorithm.variant: quantum phase estimation on a rank-1 projector to identify the desired eigenstate and estimate normalization
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start from an approximate state |~ψ> = sqrt(λ)|ψ> + sqrt(1-λ)|ψ_perp> and a uniform ancilla |+>^⊗m

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same discretized function-state encoding as the main method; phase estimation is applied to U(t)=exp(-it/N |φ><φ|)
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the normalization factor and/or project onto the desired function state |ψ> using QPE
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on non-zero phase-estimation outcome; success probability depends on overlap with target state
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Projector Hamiltonian |ψ><ψ| (implemented via low-rank simulation of |φ><φ|/N)
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: m ancilla qubits for phase estimation

problem_instance.description: Generic continuous-function state preparation and normalization estimation; no specific dataset beyond the same continuous functions used elsewhere in the paper

dataset_specification.description: Continuous function on [a,b] discretized on an n-qubit grid

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare an approximate state and use controlled time evolutions U(t)^{2^k} followed by inverse QFT
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical derivation of success probability and expected number of trials; no hardware experiment

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical choice of t and preparation of an approximate input state
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla register; if non-zero, infer normalization factor from observed phase γ0

speedup_claims.factor: exponential improvement in normalization-factor estimation / integration
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical numerical quadrature or sampling-based normalization
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming error-free projector evolution and sufficiently large t; gate-based quantum computer
speedup_claims.caveats: Success probability depends on overlap λ and filling ratio F; algorithmic error from projector simulation is not included in the idealized derivation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Expected trials scale as O(1/λ); state-preparation subroutine inherits the paper’s O(F^p/ϵ^2) simulation cost for projector evolution
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical normalization/integration would generally require numerical quadrature or sampling; not quantified
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Depends on overlap λ and filling ratio F
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: m controlled evolutions plus inverse QFT per phase-estimation run

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not assessed; no benchmarked crossover size reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: m ancilla qubits for QPE; controlled-U ladder and inverse QFT; expected trials scale as O(1/λ).
limiting_factors: Success probability depends on overlap λ

experiments.description: Single-ancilla destructive-interference state-preparation and verification circuit for continuous functions.

algorithm.variant: destructive interference / reflection-based state preparation and verification
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start from an approximate state or the all-plus state; apply a sign-flip evolution on the target component

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same n-qubit discretized function-state encoding; one ancilla qubit controls a reflection about |ψ>
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |ψ> by interfering an approximate state with its reflected version and post-selecting ancilla |1>
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on ancilla |1>; can be used as a verification filter for adiabatic output

problem_instance.description: Generic continuous-function state preparation and verification; no specific dataset beyond the same function families

dataset_specification.description: Continuous function on [a,b] discretized on an n-qubit grid

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use an approximate state |~ψ> and a controlled evolution e^{-iπ|ψ><ψ|}
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical success-probability derivation; no hardware experiment

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preparation of an approximate input state and choice of reflection time
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla; if |1>, obtain |ψ>; otherwise restart

speedup_claims.factor: single-ancilla verification / state preparation with polynomially bounded success probability
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical verification or repeated approximate preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: gate-based quantum computer; good approximate input state; filling ratio F not too small
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an appendix algorithmic variant; no hardware experiment. Error bound depends on F and repetition count r.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Algorithmic error O(F^p/r) after r repetitions; success probability λ for a good approximate input state
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Depends on filling ratio F and initial-state fidelity λ
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: One reflection circuit per attempt; repeated until ancilla success

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Single ancilla qubit plus projector evolution; success probability equals fidelity λ.
limiting_factors: Depends on having a good approximate input state

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start from smaller-k state and iteratively add qubits using conditional rotations
